title: Server exited unexpectedly using neovim 0.10.0 over SSH in terminals that support sixel
body:
### Issue description

Running tmux in Alacritty then SSHing into a client and running neovim 0.10.0 will crash the tmux server.

* Running tmux in urxvt and doing the same does not cause the issue.
* SSHing into a server with neovim 0.9.5 and doing the same does not cause the issue.
* I've tested both with my personal tmux config as well as vanilla (logs below are using my personal config, let me know if you need vanilla)

In case this was due to the new osc52 support for copy/paste, I tried disabling osc52 in the alacritty config but there was no difference. I also attempted to prevent osc52 copy/paste in neovim by forcing unnamedplus (which the documentation says prevents the feature from loading) but still hit the issue.

Describe the problem and the steps to reproduce:

1. Start tmux in Alacritty
2. SSH into a box with neovim 0.10
3. Run `nvim -u NORC` (to load without any config)
4. Observe `[server exited unexpectedly]`

### Required information

Please provide the following information:

* tmux version: 3.4 (from the Archlinux repos)
* Platform: Linux unknown (Archlinux)
* Inside tmux: tmux-256color -- Outside tmux: alacritty
* Logs:
    [tmux-client-607371.log](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/files/15353857/tmux-client-607371.log)
    [tmux-out-607375.log](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/files/15353858/tmux-out-607375.log)
    [tmux-server-607375.log](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/files/15353859/tmux-server-607375.log)

Let me know if you need additional information and I'd be happy to provide it. Also, thanks for maintaining tmux :)

My steps to reproduce

1. `tmux -vv -f /dev/null -L test new`
2. ssh onto a remote machine with neovim 0.10 (`NVIM v0.10.0` from linuxbrew)
3. Start neovim with no custom config: `nvim -u NONE`

I've tested this with both the following setups:

* (to test on a mac) tmux on my mac → ssh onto linux server A → start nvim → local tmux crashes
* (to test on a linux) ssh onto linux server J → start tmux → ssh onto linux server A → start nvim → tmux on server J crashes

### Required information

* tmux version (`tmux -V`): `tmux 3.4` on both my mac and linux server J
* Platform (`uname -sp`). `Darwin arm` and `Linux x86_64`
* $TERM inside and outside of tmux (`echo $TERM`).
  * on my mac: `screen-256color` inside and `xterm-256color` outside
  * on linux server J: `tmux-256color` inside and `xterm-256color` outside

The last few lines of tmux server logs look like this:


Observe the same behavior when opening a file in neovim via sudo in a tmux session:

```sh
$ tmux
$ touch file.txt
$ sudo nvim file.txt
[server exited unexpectedly]
```

However, can confirm that the workaround suggested by @participant7 does not crash tmux:
```sh
$ tmux
$ sudo -E TMUX=$TMUX nvim file.txt
```

comments.body:
# Issue
Similar to everyone's stated issue of tmux server unexpectedly exiting, but slightly different variables and setup.

## Setup and Versions
Local Tmux: 3.4 on Manjaro
Remote Tmux: 3.4 on Ubuntu
Remote Nvim:
```
NVIM v0.10.0
Build type: Release
LuaJIT 2.1.1713484068
```
I also have fairly developed `.ssh/configs` and `.tmux.conf` files, but I do not think those affect anything relevant (of course, I could be mistaken).

## Scenarios
### The Crash/Exit
The setup that gave me the exit is a tmux server locally and then a ssh to a GCP instance. From there, I ran `nvim` and it crashes/exits.
In the local tmux, the `$TMUX` var is pointed to the file you'd expect. After ssh-ing to the remote instance, `$TMUX` is empty. Setting it to an arbitrary value doesn't prevent the crash/exit.

### Preventing Crash/Exit and Strange Output
 If I create a tmux session locally and then ssh to my remote instance and then run `nvim -V` I get repeating output:
```
...
chdir(vim/)                                                                                                                                                                                 
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(vim/)                                                                                                                                                                                 
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(/home/<user>/apps/nvim-linux64/share/nvim/runtime/lua/vim/)                                                                                                 
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(/home/<user>)                                                                                                                                               
chdir(vim/)                                                                                                                                                                                 
-- More --[server exited unexpectedly]
```
where it eventually exits after scrolling some number of lines (~40ish).

More interestingly, I can prevent the exit/crash by running this:
```
nvim -V | less
```
less doesn't really work correctly, but captures some of the output. I can then exit less where I am still stuck in the nvim command (I think) and then can Ctrl-C out of the command with my tmux session still intact. A return code of 0 is given:
```
❯ echo $?
0
```
Also `nvim | less` produces the same behavior.

### No Crash/Exit
What if I nest tmux sessions so the `$TMUX` variable is set on the remote machine?:
```
ssh work-bastion -t tmux new -t work -s work
```
It works (mostly). I can run nvim on a file or just plainly, but the interesting part is when I use `nvim -V`. I get the strange output as above, except I make it all the way to the very end of output:
```
...
chdir(/home/<user>)

Executing BufEnter Autocommands for "*"                                                                                                                                                     
autocommand sil call s:LocalBrowse(expand("<amatch>"))                                                                                                                                      
Executing VimEnter Autocommands for "*"                                                                                                                                                     
Press ENTER or type command to continue                                                                                                                                                     
autocommand sil call s:VimEnter(expand("<amatch>"))                                                                                                                                         
Press ENTER or type command to continue                                                                                                                                                     
Press ENTER or type command to continue
```
If I hit `e` I enter nvim edit mode? Or at least I enter nvim's main page and can then exit if I press the right keys, which is some weird mix of nvim commands and whatever the hell command line mode I am in above.
